Janow Lubelski Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Janów Lubelski, Poland

Demolished. Janów Lubelski's Jewish community, present from a 1652 privilege permitting settlement, grew to 3,385 people (52 percent of the town) by 1904. During Operation Reinhardt in 1942, about 300 Jews were murdered in Janów Lubelski and the rest deported to the Bełżec death camp. This, the older of the town's two Jewish cemeteries, was completely destroyed during WWII; a 1950s construction project on the site uncovered human remains, which were reburied in the town's Catholic cemetery at an unmarked location.
